items.snippet: Yemen's Houthi group has released 159 prisoners under an amnesty issued by its leadership, describing them as fighters who voluntarily surrendered during recent clashes. The announcement was made in Sanaa by Abdul Qader al-Murtada, head of the group's prisoner affairs committee. items.title: Apple opens preorders for iPhone Duo, testing demand for foldables
items.snippet: CNBC’s MacKenzie Sigalos reports on consumer demand for Apple’s iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable phone, as preorders open.

items.title: U.S. budget deficit swells to almost $2 trillion for fiscal 2026, up 12% in a single year
items.snippet: The Treasury Department said the U.S. budget deficit came in at nearly $2 trillion for the 2026 fiscal year. CNBC's Steve Liesman has the numbers.

items.title: What we know so far about the OpenAI bugging suspect
items.snippet: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a “sophisticated recording device” was discovered inside an executive conference room at the company, according to the Department of Justice. CNBC's Eamon Javers breaks down what we know so far about Abdulrahman Alfozan, who is a national of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and was fired from OpenAI after the incident.
